variantChange.name: channel-transmission-loss
variantChange.source: NRCS NEH Part 630 Ch. 19 Transmission Losses (210-VI-NEH, Aug 2007) Table 19C-2, Wilson, DeCook & Neuman (1980) from Matlock (1965) streamflow data: "Average for Tucson area" effective hydraulic conductivity 1.65 in/h (reach ranges: Santa Cruz 1.5-3.4 and 3.2-3.7, Rillito 0.5-3.3 and 2.2-5.5, Pantano 1.6-2.0 in/h); bed group 3 of Table 19-1 (sand and gravel, low silt-clay, 1.0-3.0 in/h); Walnut Gulch fitted K 1.03-1.55 in/h (Table 19C-1, Lane, Ferreira & Shirley 1980)
variantChange.solverRoute: SFINCS f3647fc sfincs_urban_drainage.f90 injection_well: qd = min(injection_rate*A_cell/A_zone, z_volume/dt) on wet cells, removed from the model; runs alongside inftype cnb

priorVariantChanges.name: cnb-recovery
priorVariantChanges.source: SFINCS f3647fc inftype cnb (SCS CN with SWMM recovery, eqs 4-36/4-37): smax = base GCN10 cn_f_ii_2281 (fair, ARC II, undrained) S in m (unchanged CN source); seff = smax (dry start 2026-10-30 16Z); ks = POLARIS v1.0 ksat mean 0-5 cm (Chaney et al. 2019, doi:10.1029/2018WR022797) face-area mean, mm/hr, HydroMT-SFINCS 1.2.2 360 mm/hr cap (none capped)

infiltrationChange.label: SENSITIVITY infiltration 2: SCS Curve Number WITH recovery (SFINCS inftype cnb) instead of cna; not tuned to observations; not for live registration
infiltrationChange.hypothesis: cna accumulates all rain from 2026-10-30T16Z as one storm (91% of the Black Wash area past Ia before the Nov 1 14Z burst); cnb starts a new event after each dry spell with S recovered at the SWMM rate, so the Oct 30-Nov 1 showers stop counting as the start of the Nov 1 storm
infiltrationChange.solver: SFINCS f3647fc source/src/sfincs_infiltration.f90 initialize_infiltration_cnb / compute_infiltration_cnb: per face, new event when prcp>0 after a dry step (P1=0, S1=Se); Q=(P1-0.2 S1)^2/(P1+0.8 S1); Se -= infiltration; when dry, after 0.06/kr hours Se += kr*Smax per hour up to Smax; kr = sqrt(ks[mm/hr]/25.4)/75 per hour (SWMM Reference Manual Vol I, eqs 4-36, 4-37). Rain frames are linearly interpolated in time, so a dry spell starts only between two zero frames.

smax.source: base case scs (GCN10 cn_f_ii_2281, fair, ARC II, undrained, inches) * 0.0254; CN source unchanged

seff.choice: seff = smax (fully dry start at tstart 2026-10-30T16Z)
seff.evidence: NCEP Stage IV (IEM archive) over the model box: 24h totals ending 12Z Oct 24..29 domain mean 0.00-0.04 mm (max cell 0.6 mm); 24h ending Oct 30 12Z mean 2.53 mm (max 15 mm); Oct 30 12-16Z mean 1.15 mm (hourly cell maxima 4.6 and 7.1 mm). That ~3.7 mm is not counted (same as the cna base), so the start is slightly too dry (at most ~7% of mean Smax 56 mm).

ks.source: POLARIS v1.0 ksat mean 0-5 cm (Chaney et al. 2019, Water Resour. Res. 55, doi:10.1029/2018WR022797), http://hydrology.cee.duke.edu/POLARIS/PROPERTIES/v1.0/ksat/mean/0_5/ tiles lat3132/lat3233_lon-112-111, log10(cm/hr) -> mm/hr, face-area arithmetic mean, HydroMT-SFINCS 1.2.2 cap 360 mm/hr (0 faces capped), no NaN, no fill

channelLossChange.label: SENSITIVITY channel transmission loss; not tuned to observations; not for live registration
channelLossChange.hypothesis: Routed flood water soaks into the sandy wash beds (transmission loss), which the rain-only cnb infiltration cannot represent; removing it at a published Tucson-area rate should lower the Mile Wide (ALERT 6443) volume and peak
channelLossChange.source: NRCS NEH Part 630 Ch. 19 (Aug 2007) Table 19C-2 (Wilson, DeCook & Neuman 1980; Matlock 1965): Tucson-area average 1.65 in/h; Table 19-1 group 3 sand-gravel low silt-clay 1.0-3.0 in/h; Walnut Gulch fitted K 1.03-1.55 in/h (Table 19C-1)
channelLossChange.solver: SFINCS f3647fc source/src/sfincs_urban_drainage.f90 injection_well: qmax(nm)=injection_rate*A(nm)/A_zone; qd=min(qmax, z_volume/dt) when zs > subgrid_z_zmin; qsrc -= qd; removed from the model; independent of inftype
channelLossChange.where: faces (msk 1) whose centre is inside .sfincs-runs/brawley-avra-west-parameters-v2n/channel-mask.geojson (order>=3 NHD, lidar half-depth width, lidar-centred)
channelLossChange.rate: zone injection_rate = K x area(channel mask within the zone cells), so the loss is K on the bed area, spread over the zone cells when wet
